text: huh ok so just verify then what is the difference between that approach and the in-studio key modifiers like shift, that do work
resolution: Verified the difference between the working in-studio shift and the dead world-viewport shift-click. Studio: mesh-editor input is NATIVE — engine.zig intercepts the raw SDL mouse event in the frame loop (4438), and when the click is viewport (not chrome) it reads SDL_GetModState() in place (4500) and passes shift directly to r3d.meshEditPick / meshEditBox (4502/4976); the modifier never crosses a boundary. World viewport: a React component whose clicks go through the JS event bridge — the runtime reconstructs the event from host getters (runtime/index.tsx getPointerPayload) and modifier state was never packed into that reconstruction, so it drops at the border. Same SDL event, two delivery paths; keyboard events pack mods, mouse events never did. Matches the repo doctrine that native-input surfaces work by construction while JS-picked surfaces inherit bridge gaps. Q&A only, no code changed.
